notes:
Summary: LexGuard provides enterprise e-discovery and legal document review for top-100 law firms. Exploring Redwood for a next-gen RAG pipeline: dense embeddings + reranking to improve precision on precedent retrieval. Key constraints: must run in customer VPC/private control plane, 7-year retention for audit trails, and tamper-evident audit logs.

Why Redwood: team emphasized unified runtime + private deployment path. Interested in dedicated pools for predictable throughput during large review jobs.

Scale & indexing: customer expects initial corpus of ~120M documents (emails, PDFs, discovery bundles). Estimated embedding vectors ~120M - plan to shard index by matter/client. Warm-up ingestion test requested: 10M docs over 48 hours.

Latency & throughput targets: interactive lawyer-facing search: p95 < 300ms (end-to-end, including reranker). Batch review queries (legal analytics): sustained throughput 250 qps with 200ms median per-query. Cost sensitivity: target blended cost/query <$0.05 for production; willing to accept higher during heavy discovery windows.

Retrieval + reranking architecture preferences: dense retrieval (ANN) for recall, followed by cross-encoder reranker for precision on first-page results. Want ability to pin reranker to higher-cost GPU pool (dedicated) while keeping ANN on cheaper nodes. Must support partial-fallback to smaller quantized models when capacity constrained.

Security/Compliance specifics: SSO/SAML integration mandatory; audit log retention >= 7 years; immutable retention windows per client matter; per-token and per-query access auditing; KMS integration (customer-managed keys preferred) and HSM option for private deployment. Data residency: US-only for given clients.

POC ask: 1) VPC private control plane deployment blueprint; 2) ingest 500k test docs and run search/rerank benchmark (latency, QPS, cost) with Redwood Optimize suggestions; 3) show audit log format and retention demo.

Quotes/bullets from calls: 
- "We need tamper-evident audit trails for every review session."
- "If latency slips above 300ms for lawyers, adoption will stall."
- "Cost per query is a KPI for our operations team — show us unit economics."

Internal notes: SE recommended layered caching (prefix KV) and reranker pinning; engineering asked for sample seq-length distributions and typical query templates. Legal sent initial questionnaire (SEC-6019).
